Article Title: 'They are from his film fan base': Congress MLA brushes aside TVK’s 'Vijay for PM' pitch
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert on Wednesday dismissed ally TVK’s projection of its leader, C Joseph Vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, saying TVK leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to Vijay’s past as an actor.“They are TVK MLAs, they are all still in the fan basis. They have come from a fan--film industries as a fan basis. Definitely, they will be saying that,” Cuthbert told reporters in Chennai.She added that, politically, the leaders had taken a “stern decision” that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi would be the candidate for the prime minister’s post in 2029.Cuthbert’s remarks come amid growing differences over the political positioning of the two parties, with TVK leaders repeatedly projecting Vijay as a possible national leader.TVK leader and Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier asserted that the country’s top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.Responding to the remarks by TVK leaders, Congress leader and state Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar warned that the two Congress ministers in the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government would resign if the Vijay-led party did not accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate.The Congress ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and extended support to TVK, which emerged as the single-largest party but fell short of the majority mark. The Congress backed TVK along with the VCK, IUML, CPI and CPI(M), with the stated condition that “communal forces” be kept out of the government.Vijay launched TVK in February 2024, becoming the latest Tamil film star to enter state politics.The Congress last led a government at the Centre from 2004 to 2014.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert dismissed ally TVK’s projection of its leader, C Joseph Vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. She said TVK leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to Vijay's past as an actor. The Congress ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and extended support to TVK.

Article Title: Changes in pre- and post-SIR voter lists prove poll theft by BJP: Rahul
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi (ANI image)

NEW DELHI: Citing huge variations in the pre- and post-SIR voter lists, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the draft in Maharashtra and the revised Bengal lists prove his allegation that elections in those states were stolen by BJP.Dubbing Election Commission "vote chori commission", Rahul said EC and BJP keep changing their tactics but their sole objective is "BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of democracy."Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said EC included a large number of voters ahead of the assembly elections in Delhi, and has now dropped over 47 lakh voters from the draft list while preparing to send notices to over 30 lakh more. "Congress workers are facing manipulations daily in Telangana and Karnataka as well," he said.Rahul said in Maharashtra, 39 lakh new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections in 2024. "... Now in Maharashtra, 2.1 crore voters have been removed from the draft list - that's every fifth voter. Lok Sabha 2024: 9.3 crore, Vidhan Sabha 2024: 9.7 crore, SIR 2026: 7.8 crore. Which list was correct?" he asked. Rahul said in Bengal, 91% of all the names removed from the voters' list after SIR ahead of the 2026 assembly polls has been reinstated. "That means 9 out of every 10 names were wrongly deleted, and added back only after the election... This was vote theft."
Article Summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the draft in Maharashtra and the revised Bengal lists prove his allegation that elections in those states were stolen by BJP. Rahul said EC and BJP keep changing their tactics but their sole objective is "BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of democracy"

Article Title: Sudhikaran row: BJP SC Morcha performs ‘buddhi-shuddhi’ ritual for Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
Image credit: PTI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The political row over the alleged purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground following Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally last month has intensified, with the BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha performing a ‘buddhi-shuddhi’ ritual for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Panchayati Temple in Dehradun.The development came as Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal led a massive protest march towards the state Secretariat, condemning the alleged ‘purification’ ritual conducted after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's August 8 rally in Haldwani.Accompanied by AICC co-in-charges Surendra Sharma and Manoj Yadav and hundreds of Congress workers, Godiyal attempted to gherao the Secretariat. Heavy police deployment was made to disperse the protesters, while several workers were detained as they raised slogans.The controversy centres on allegations that a ‘suddhikaran yajna’ was conducted at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground after Kharge's address. Congress leaders have criticised the alleged ritual, calling it an insult to the party president and an instance of caste discrimination."The rally happened in Haldwani, and then that place has a suddhikaran and havan. Then, the BJP State President justifies it and says that it is okay.What else could be more shameless?...BJP is working on the RSS agenda," Uttarakhand Assembly Leader of Opposition Yashpal Arya told ANI.The controversy also led to an FIR against Rahul Gandhi following a complaint by a member of the Scheduled Caste community, who alleged that the Congress leader's remarks about the purification ritual hurt the sentiments of the community.According to the complaint, members of the Valmiki community participated in cleaning the venue and conducting the ritual after the Congress rally attended by Kharge and other leaders.Godiyal, along with Surendra Sharma, Manoj Yadav and Congress workers, had also reached Dehradun's Kotwali Police Station on Monday seeking registration of an FIR against those responsible for the Haldwani incident.The row has since spread beyond Uttarakhand, with Congress units in several states protesting over the alleged ritual. Rahul Gandhi and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi have also criticised the incident, describing it as a manifestation of a "Manuvadi mindset" and alleging that it was an attempt to demean a Dalit leader.The BJP has denied involvement in the ceremony. Union Minister and Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the act in Parliament, saying the BJP had no association with the organisers and that the matter would be investigated.The organisers, Shri Ram Sena, along with local BJP representatives, maintained that the havan was not conducted because of Kharge's caste. They claimed the ritual was performed because religious decorum had allegedly been violated at the Ramlila Ground.
Article Summary: BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha performs 'buddhi-shuddhi' ritual for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at Panchayati Temple in Dehradun. Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal led a massive protest march towards the state Secretariat, condemning the alleged ‘purification’ ritual conducted after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's rally.

Article Title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs
Article Text:
TMC rebel MPs after attending the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) Parliamentary Party Meeting (ANI photo)

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI and sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that lays down the anti-defection framework.Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.In a post on X, TMC Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra shared the photo of one of the notices issued to rebel MPs and said, “Cover up caught out!” Highlighting that TMC had filed 20 disqualification petitions in June, Moitra said, “Speaker LS did nothing except give them better seats at our expense. SG Tushar Mehta in Court said the Speaker had issued notices. Notice dated Aug 25th -- exact date of hearing!”On Tuesday, Supreme Court sought a response from Lok Sabha Speaker’s office on time-bound adjudication of TMC’s petition seeking disqualification of rebel MPs who broke away from the party after its electoral debacle in West Bengal, even as Abhishek Banerjee accused Speaker Om Birla of “deliberate inaction”.The SC also issued notices to the 20 rebel MPs: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachna Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Abu Teher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Kalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.In his petition, Abhishek Banerjee told the court on Tuesday that he had lodged the disqualification petition against the rebel MPs on June 18 and complained that despite the lapse of two months, no meaningful progress has been made on its adjudication.The continuing delay in the adjudication process is impacting democratic governance, he said.In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June. Banerjee had earlier met Birla on July 27 in Parliament urging him to expedite his decision on the pending petitions.
Article Summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI. The notices sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification.

Article Title: Rahul or Vijay for PM? Congress-TVK rift talk grows after MLA’s seat shift
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay

NEW DELHI: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday after Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly.This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the state cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Speaking at an event in Kanyakumari on Saturday, Kumar said Rahul Gandhi would become the Prime Minister in 2029.The remarks came amid statements by TVK leaders projecting party chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential contender for the PM's post. TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier said the country's top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan questioned why the Congress continued to be part of the TVK government despite the differences over the prime ministerial candidate."Repeated assertions by multiple TVK Ministers even inside on the floor of the Tamil Nadu Assembly touting their leader as a probable Prime Minister is an outright rejection of the failed and dismal leadership of Rahul Gandhi by the TVK.Now, what is preventing the opportunistic Congress party from coming out of the cabinet of the TVK government? Because the TVK minister's statements are a scathing vote of no confidence, and TVK is an alliance partner, but the Congress party still continues to be in the TVK government.Why is the Congress party not withdrawing support to the TVK government after their leader Rahul Gandhi has been insulted?" news agency ANI quoted Kesavan saying.The issue has gained further attention after a private media survey placed Vijay among the preferred candidates for PM in 2029, behind PM Narendra Modi and Rahul Gandhi.The TVK government was formed after the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, when the party emerged as the largest force and formed the government with support from VCK, IUML, Congress, CPI and CPI(M).

Article Title: ​Govt delegation delays its visit to meet Jarange

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: 3,400 SIR forms found at Navi Mumbai photocopy shop; 5 BLOs suspended as Sena (UBT)-BJP clash
Article Text:
Authorities seized numerous printed Special Intensive Revision forms from the premises

THANE/MUMBAI: Five Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were suspended after 3,400 enumeration forms related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls were found at a private photocopy shop in Navi Mumbai’s Kharghar, triggering a political confrontation between Shiv Sena (UBT) and BJP workers and prompting an administrative inquiry, police and district officials said.The forms, which were filled by voters from the Panvel Assembly constituency, were found at a photocopy centre in Sector 19 following complaints that SIR applications were being photocopied there and that a person associated with the BJP youth wing was allegedly in unauthorised possession of them.Police rushed to the shop and took Suraj Patil, who was allegedly getting the forms photocopied, into custody.Authorities also seized thousands of printed SIR forms from the premises and shifted them to the police station, news agency PTI reported.he controversy came to light after a video related to the incident went viral on Thursday.The administration subsequently ordered an inquiry into how forms filled by voters reached a private photocopy centre.Following the complaint, the Electoral Registration Officer deputed Assistant Electoral Registration Officers to inspect the photocopy centre.During the inspection, officials found that Patil had brought 3,400 applications to the shop.Scrutiny showed that the forms belonged to 11 polling stations. A majority of the applications were from five polling stations, while single copies were found from six other polling stations.Shiv Sena (UBT) workers had confronted Patil at the shop, alleging that he was a BJP Youth Wing office-bearer. BJP workers, however, denied any connection with the matter.Sena (UBT) workers also alleged that Patil managed to flee the Kharghar police station shortly after being taken there for questioning.Raigad district collector Kishan Jawale on Friday said a case had been registered against Patil under the Representation of the People Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Jawale visited the office of Panvel Sub-Divisional Officer Pawan Chandak and said the five BLOs had been suspended pending disciplinary proceedings.Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer Balesh Bhojane questioned how SIR forms filled by ordinary voters could have reached private individuals and alleged that BJP youth wing functionaries were linked to the incident.Panvel Municipal Corporation mayor and BJP leader Nitin Patil, however, said party workers had no connection with the matter.Opposition NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said suspending the five BLOs was not enough and alleged that the incident exposed problems in the way the SIR process was being conducted."We have been saying that the BJP is using this process to ensure its poll victory and this incident proves us right," he said.Pawar said he had sought a response from the Election Commission over the incident, but the authorities had passed the responsibility to the Election Commission of India."Suspending only the BLOs is not enough. The authorities who instructed them should also be suspended, and action should be taken against the BJP workers involved," Pawar added.He also said there could be many similar incidents that had not been detected and sought a response from the Election Commission.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: 5 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) suspended after 3,400 enumeration forms found at private photocopy shop in Navi Mumbai’s Kharghar. Police took Suraj Patil, who was allegedly getting the forms photocopied, into custody. Authorities also seized thousands of printed SIR forms from the premises.

Article Title: Congress will oppose delimitation exercise, says former CM Prithviraj Chavan
Article Text:
Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan

Nashik

:





Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan on Tuesday said Congress would oppose Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise, irrespective of whether Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) chose to support it.“Centre should avoid undertaking the exercise without broad political consensus. It should take all stakeholders into confidence before taking any decision on delimitation,” Chavan said, while speaking to reporters in Nashik ahead of Rahul Gandhi ’s visit on Wednesday.Chavan was in the city ahead of the concluding session of a 10-day training camp for Congress district presidents from Maharashtra. Gandhi is scheduled to address the closed-door programme on Wednesday at MTDC’s Grape Park Resort near Gangapur dam.Raising questions over the transparency of projects linked to the Simhastha Kumbh Mela, Chavan said Congress had sought the detailed project report (DPR) for the proposed works but had not received it so far. While supporting govt’s planned expenditure of Rs 34,000 crore on Kumbh-related infrastructure, he said the funds must be used to create durable civic assets rather than temporary facilities.“We are not opposed to spending Rs 34,000 crore on Kumbh Mela works. The investment should create permanent infrastructure and contribute to Nashik’s long-term development. Govt must also focus on accelerating the city’s industrial growth,” he said.Targeting BJP , Chavan claimed the ruling party had entered a “panic mode” following recent protests by Gen Z youth in Delhi and was increasingly concerned about the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He alleged that BJP was even considering advancing the general elections to 2028.Chavan also claimed Prime Minister Narendra Modi was facing resistance over a proposed Union cabinet reshuffle. According to him, three Union ministers, including Nitin Gadkari and Rajnath Singh, were likely to be replaced but had opposed the move.On the education front, the former CM stressed the need for a full-time Union education minister, saying the portfolio was currently being handled as an additional charge by Union minister Pralhad Joshi. “There is no Union education minister with the national stature and credibility required to engage with students and address growing concerns over the examination system,” Chavan added.
Article Summary: Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan said Congress would oppose Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise. Chavan was in the city ahead of the concluding session of a 10-day training camp for Congress district presidents from Maharashtra. Rahul Gandhi is scheduled to address the closed-door programme on Wednesday.

Article Title: I am constitutionally bound to accept voluntary resignation of MLA, TamilNadu assembly speaker tells Madras high court
Article Text:
J C D Prabhakar





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu assembly speaker J C D Prabhakar on Tuesday informed the Madras high court that he is constitutionally duty bound to accept the resignation tendered by an MLA if it is done voluntarily. No one can compel a legislator to continue in his/her post, he said.Senior advocate C S Vaidyanathan and advocate-general Vijay Narayan made the submission on behalf of the speaker while opposing the pleas challenging his decision in accepting the resignation of six AIADMK MLAs before deciding the disqualification proceedings for cross voting in favour of the TVK govt violating party whip.Recording the submissions, the first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan reserved their orders. The petitions were filed by AIADMK whip Agri S S Krishnamurthy and others.Acceptance of the resignations would not automatically render the pending disqualification proceedings ineffective. If an MLA wishes to resign, he or she cannot be compelled to continue in office. Refusal to accept such resignations would amount to a failure on the part of the speaker to discharge a constitutional duty, Vaidyanathan said.“The speaker could inquire only whether the resignations were submitted voluntarily.The other aspects of whether the MLAs resigned in exchange for a ministerial position or money, or whether horse-trading had taken place, could be examined only as part of the disqualification proceedings,” he added.The purpose or motive behind a resignation could not be examined while deciding whether to accept it, he said.Representing the MLAs, senior advocates Satish Parasaran and Menaka Guruswamy contended that defection proceedings would arise only if an MLA continued to enjoy the privileges of office while extending support to another political party. Resigning from the office of MLA and subsequently joining another political party constitute democratic political activity, they said.Senior counsel V V Giri and S R Rajagopal for Krishnamurthy submitted that conducting an inquiry to ascertain whether the resignations were made voluntarily or not was not merely a procedural formality but a constitutional obligation, and that no meaningful inquiry had actually been conducted.
Article Summary: No one can compel a legislator to continue in his/her post, he said. The purpose or motive behind a resignation could not be examined while deciding whether to accept it. The petitions were filed by AIADMK whip Agri S S Krishnamurthy and others.

Article Title: Two women killed as car rams bike near Srivaikuntam in Thoothukudi
Article Text:
Two women killed as car rams bike near Srivaikuntam in Thoothukudi





Thoothukudi: Two women were killed after a car rammed into the two-wheeler they were travelling on near Mudivaithanenthal in Thoothukudi district on Tuesday.Police identified the deceased as Sathya , 40, of Thiruvalluvar Colony, and Amutha, 45, of Nazareth. Police said the duo were riding to Srivaikuntam on the Thoothukudi-Srivaikuntam road. When they were nearing the Mudivaithanendal tank, a speeding car rammed into the two-wheeler from behind. Both women suffered severe head injuries and died on the spot, police said.Police sent the bodies to a govt hospital for postmortem examination. They registered a case against the car driver, Saravanan , 31, of Nazareth, and arrested him. Further investigation is on.
Article Summary: Two women killed as car rams bike near Srivaikuntam in Thoothukudi district. Police identified the deceased as Sathya, 40, and Amutha, 45, of Nazareth. Both women suffered severe head injuries and died on the spot, police said.

Article Title: Murder accused escapes police custody in Madurai
Article Text:
Murder accused escapes police custody in Madurai

Madurai

:





An accused in the murder of a Class X boy in Sivaganga on June 5 escaped from police custody near Yanaikkal junction in Madurai on Tuesday evening.The accused, Aravind , 24, from Ilanthaimangalam in Sivaganga district, was returning to Madurai Central Prison with two escort police personnel after appearing before the Sivaganga court for a hearing when he escaped.Police sources said the two-wheeler carrying Aravind and the escort personnel stopped near Yanaikkal junction around 5pm. Aravind allegedly pushed the two escort officers, jumped off the vehicle and fled.Vilakkuthoon police registered a case and launched a search to trace him.Aravind was arrested by Sivaganga district police along with a 17-year-old boy in connection with the sexual assault and murder of a Class X boy near the Keel Kaavanoor irrigation tank on June 5. The victim was found dead with his throat slit.Police said Aravind was in a relationship with the deceased boy and that he and the minor allegedly conspired to murder him after he disclosed their homosexual relationship to others. Investigators said Aravind and the victim had consumed liquor before the murder.The case came to light after a boy who witnessed the incident approached the police and shared details of the crime.Based on a complaint from the deceased’s father, Keelasevalpatti police registered a case under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and relevant provisions of the POCSO Act Aravind was lodged in Madurai Central Prison, while the minor was sent to a government observation home.
Article Summary: Accused in the murder of a Class X boy in Sivaganga on June 5 escaped from police custody near Yanaikkal junction in Madurai on Tuesday evening. The accused, Aravind, 24, from Ilanthaimangalam, was returning to Madurai Central Prison with two escort police personnel after appearing before a court. He allegedly pushed the two escort officers, jumped off the vehicle and fled.

Article Title: Thoothukudi firing: Will TVK govt reopen cases against 3 top officials?
Article Text:
file picture





Madurai: Madras high court on Monday sought the TVK govt’s stand on re-examining the decisions taken by the previous govt to drop disciplinary action against three officials -- the then Thoothukudi district collector N Venkatesh, then inspector-general of police Shailesh Kumar Yadav and then DIG of police Kapil Kumar C Saratkar -- in connection with the police firing on anti-Sterlite protestors in Thoothukudi in 2018.Pursuant to the earlier order, the state filed a compliance report before the court stating that it was under the previous DMK govt further action was dropped in the disciplinary proceedings initiated against the three officials. Taking into account the report, a division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel sought response from the present TVK govt with regard to re-examining the decisions taken by the previous govt to drop the disciplinary action.Earlier, the court directed the state to file detailed reports on documents relating to Justice Aruna Jagadeesan Commission, action taken on the commission’s report and relief granted to the family members of the victims.The court passed the order while hearing a batch of petitions filed in 2018 pertaining to the Tuticorin police firing incident. The petitioners sought a direction to initiate action against the erring officials responsible for the death of 13 people in the incident. The matter was adjourned to Sept 10.
Article Summary: Madras high court sought TVK govt’s stand on re-examining the decisions taken by the previous govt to drop disciplinary action against three officials. The three officials were involved in the police firing on anti-Sterlite protestors in Thoothukudi in 2018.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.
